page: Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running on AWS Graviton4 processors with ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 384 GB of memory, which establishes a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor topology allocates 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 36 MB L3 cache. It contains hardware acceleration for cryptographic operations via ARM AES instructions, but does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and high-capacity memory bandwidth, contrasting with middle-tier single-core performance. In stress-ng benchmarks, multi-core CPU performance reaches the top 10% tier at 314,126.93, while single-core processing remains average at 1,643.69. Memory subsystems record high throughput, achieving 907.46 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 403.08 GB/sec for uncached writes. Parallel workloads show high performance margins, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1,380.75 GB/sec, Clang compilation scores of 87,655.0, and 355.18 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff of the c8g.48xlarge is its reliance on remote EBS storage, as no local NVMe disks are attached to the host. In addition, its single-threaded execution performance and smaller LLM prompt processing capabilities fall into average or lower percentiles compared to x86-64 alternatives. However, the presence of 192 physical cores without simultaneous multithreading provides consistent compute density and high instruction execution without cross-thread contention.

The instance delivers high resource density for scale-out parallel workloads. Given the 50 Gbps baseline network throughput and massive multi-threaded compute capacity, the c8g.48xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, static web serving clusters, large-scale software compilation, batch processing, and compute-bound in-memory data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized bare-metal-equivalent virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System. Driven by 192 dedicated ARMv9 AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz with single-threaded physical execution, the instance is paired with 384 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput maintains a 50 Gbps baseline, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core metrics, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput, while single-thread execution and LLM prompt processing remain moderate. Operating without cross-thread execution contention, the c8g.48xlarge is suitable for highly concurrent compute workloads, parallel software builds, batch transcoding, web serving tiers, and distributed data processing operations.
